floor_history.headline: Recon s1: canonical island respell (func_800274BC form) lowered floor 33->30 with insn parity 144==144; full residual map banked; disc-copy survival is the frontier head.

s1 frontier head CLOSED: combine (not cse) folds the disc copy; an if/else-spelled LZCS guard makes it survive at zero insn cost, landing in $a0 (target's register) in the beqz delay slot. Floor still

Floor 30 -> 7 at unchanged parity 144==144: reusing sqrt_val in place for the <<9 and naming the first quotient's numerator fixed the entire downstream allocation cascade; residual is 6 slots of disc-

frontier.hypothesis: Getting `disc` allocated to $a2/$6 instead of $v1/$3 closes 6 of the remaining 7 slots and is the head of everything left.
frontier.mechanism: disc is pseudo 117, allocated FIRST of 24 allocnos because global.c's priority is roughly log2(n_refs)*n_refs/live_length and its range is only 6 insns with 5 refs; it then takes its recorded preference $3. In target, disc's bltz read (slot 96) keeps it live ~6 slots longer, which both lowers its priority (so it is not allocated first) and removes the early pick of $3. The lever is therefore to lengthen disc's live range past the copy WITHOUT adding an instruction.
frontier.next_probe: v2/v26 already proves that duplicating `ud = disc;` into both guard arms makes the bltz read disc - it just costs 2 insns because the copy is emitted twice. Probe spellings that put the copy in exactly one arm while leaving the branch on disc: (i) hoist ONLY the fast-path/slow-path split so the copy is the first statement of the slow block but the guard is evaluated before it (measure the RTL insn order in .rtl, not just the score); (ii) give disc one extra honest read AFTER the copy (e.g. route the 0x400 fast-path table index through disc while the slow path uses ud) and check whether 117 drops out of first place in the greg `regs to allocate` list; (iii) if 117 still gets $3, read set_preference's input by checking which mflo pseudo local-alloc put in $3 (dispositions line) and try re-associating the discriminant so that operand lands elsewhere.

frontier.hypothesis: Slot 88 needs `if (disc < 0) return 0;`, and the only thing stopping it is jump2 cross-jumping the resulting 2-insn block into the entrance return-0 block.
frontier.mechanism: GCC emits `(set (reg 2) 0); (jump epilogue)` for a `return 0;` statement, which is exactly target slots 87/88. jump.c's cross-jump finds the identical tail in the entrance chain and redirects the conditional branch there, deleting the block and dropping build_insns from 144 to 142. Crucially both target AND our build already carry TWO un-merged copies of that same block in the entrance chain, so cross-jump here is selective rather than exhaustive - something about the third instance makes it mergeable.
frontier.next_probe: Recompile v24 with `pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_8002D518` and read .jump2 to see WHICH pair find_cross_jump matched and why the two existing entrance copies are not merged with each other. Then try structural spellings that change the entrance chain's exit shape only where it is already byte-identical to target (it must stay byte-identical - slots 0-83 currently match), or spellings that change the disc<0 block's position relative to the entrance copies. Do NOT spend probes on respelling `return 0` itself - the emitted shape is already correct.

frontier.hypothesis: There is no third residual item - once (a) and (b) land the function is at 0.
frontier.mechanism: The v21 alignment is a complete 154-slot comparison with only 15 raw differing words, 8 of them scorer-masked classes (j-targets, %hi/%lo relocs). Every remaining word is accounted for by (a) or (b). No ordering difference, no instruction-count difference, no missing or extra instruction anywhere.
frontier.next_probe: After any change, re-run `tmp/grind/func_8002D518/s3/align.py <variant>` on an `objdump -dz` listing and confirm the raw-diff count equals engine score + 8; if it does not, a new masked class has appeared and must be identified before drawing conclusions.
